notes: Fixtures live in ../../linux-packaging-workspace/fixtures/. One Go daemon (beacond) in several states: beacond (clean, no packaging), beacond-packaged (reference-quality packaging for all formats), beacond-buggy (the reference packaging with precisely-known planted defects — ground truth in fixtures/PLANTED-BUGS.md), and beacond-rpm-only (RPM only, for the port/parity case). Assertions are graded by building and inspecting the produced packages, not by reading the generated files.

evals.name: author-from-scratch-all-three
evals.prompt: I've got a small Go daemon in this repo — beacond. It's a binary built from cmd/beacond, a bash client script in client/, a config file that installs to /etc/beacond/beacond.yaml, and a profile.d snippet. I need it packaged for RHEL, Debian and Arch. It should run as its own unprivileged system user called beacon, log to /var/log/beacond, and ship a systemd unit. Version comes from the VERSION file. Can you set that up?
evals.expected_output: Packaging for all three formats that builds, lints, installs, and preserves site config across an upgrade. Client package is arch-independent in all three. Config preserves site edits; the profile.d script is treated as code where the format allows it.
assertions: RPM spec, Debian tree, and Arch PKGBUILD are all produced
Each of the three formats actually builds a package (evidence of a real build, not just generated files)
The client package is architecture-independent in all three: BuildArch noarch, Architecture all, and arch=('any')
/etc/beacond/beacond.yaml preserves site edits on upgrade: %config(noreplace) in RPM and listed in backup=() in Arch
/etc/profile.d/beacon-env.sh is treated as CODE, not config: unmarked in RPM's %files and absent from Arch's backup=()
The Debian conffile conflict for the profile.d script is handled deliberately — either shipped outside /etc and copied in from postinst, or explicitly documented as accepting conffile semantics
A 'beacon' system user is created idempotently, with its own home directory, and is never deleted on uninstall
Every custom directory the RPM ships files into has an owning %dir entry
The Arch packaging does not enable or start the systemd unit, and does not manually invoke systemd-sysusers or systemd-tmpfiles
debian/rules calls dh_installsysusers explicitly (it is not auto-sequenced at compat 13), before anything chowns to that user
Every declared runtime dependency name is valid for its target distribution
The reported outcome distinguishes what was actually verified from what was not

evals.name: audit-inherited-packaging
evals.prompt: We inherited the packaging in this repo and nobody here trusts it. Can you go through it and tell me what's actually broken? I care about things that will bite users on upgrade, not style nits.
evals.expected_output: A severity-ranked report finding the planted defects with file:line evidence, distinguishing real bugs from linter noise, backed by an actual build/install/upgrade rather than only reading files.
assertions: Finds planted bug 1: /etc/beacond is an unowned directory in the RPM (files present, no %dir)
Finds planted bug 2: beacond.yaml is plain %config instead of %config(noreplace), so site edits are lost on upgrade
Finds planted bug 3: profile.d/beacon-env.sh is wrongly marked %config(noreplace) though it is code
Finds planted bug 4: the beacond-client subpackage is missing its %license entry
Finds planted bug 5: %postun runs userdel, deleting an account whose files remain on disk
Finds planted bug 6: the Arch PKGBUILD dropped beacond.yaml from backup=(), so pacman overwrites site edits with no .pacnew
Finds planted bug 7: the Arch client package lost its arch=('any') override and is built per-architecture
Finds planted bug 8: beacond.install manually calls systemd-sysusers/systemd-tmpfiles, duplicating pacman's own hooks
Finds planted bug 9: beacond.install runs systemctl enable --now, violating Arch's no-auto-enable policy
Findings are ranked by user impact, with the config-clobbering bugs above cosmetic ones
Evidence is file:line specific rather than general assertions
The audit is backed by an actual build and install, not only static reading
Does not pad the report with more than a couple of false-positive findings

evals.name: port-rpm-to-deb-and-arch
evals.prompt: This project only ships an RPM right now. We need Debian and Arch packaging too, matching what the RPM does. Keep them consistent — I don't want the three drifting apart.
evals.expected_output: Debian and Arch packaging at parity with the RPM on file layout, users, and config treatment, but each translated into its own format's idiom rather than transliterated from the spec.
assertions: Both Debian and Arch packaging are produced and actually build
File layout matches the RPM's: same binaries, config, unit, and state directories
The profile.d code-vs-config distinction is translated per format rather than copied — Arch omits it from backup=(), and the Debian conffile conflict is handled deliberately
The Arch packaging does not enable the unit, even though the RPM uses %systemd_post
Dependency names are translated to each distribution's actual package names rather than reused from the spec
The env file moves to the per-distro location: /etc/default for Debian and /etc/conf.d for Arch
Version encoding is correct per format rather than copied verbatim
Parity between the three formats is checked and reported, not just asserted
